title: How continuity distinguishes autonomy from agency in agentic AI
publication: Discover Artificial Intelligence
recovered_title: How continuity distinguishes autonomy from agency in agentic AI
v20_recovered_title: How continuity distinguishes autonomy from agency in agentic AI
v20_abstract: Recent discourse increasingly describes advanced artificial intelligence systems as ‘agentic’. Planning-capable language models, autonomous workflows, and multi-agent architectures are said to exhibit agency because they pursue goals, initiate actions, and coordinate behaviour over time. This article argues that such characterisations risk conflating operational autonomy with agency in the sense relevant to responsibility, authority, and governance. It accepts thin engineering uses of ‘agentic’ as a label for autonomous task execution, but rejects the normative inference that such systems are agents. Drawing on a continuity-based account, the article argues that agency in the sense relevant to responsibility, authority, and governance is not a behavioural achievement but a structural response to continuity pressure: the need to preserve a unified locus of evaluative authority across incompatible future trajectories. Optimisation, planning, and coordination presuppose such unity; they do not generate it. The account complements gradient or multi-dimensional theories of artificial agency by identifying a structural condition they presuppose but do not supply. Through cases involving LLM tool-use agents, reinforcement-learning systems, multi-agent workflows, and institutional decision systems, the article shows that systems governed by externally specified standards may optimise effectively while lacking authorship of those standards. The principal danger lies in attributing agency where continuity, authorship, and responsibility are structurally absent.

title: Toward Efficient LLM Agents for Emulator-Based Network Experiment Automation
publication: Apnet 2026 Proceedings of the 10th Asia Pacific Workshop on Networking

v20_abstract: Agent-driven scientific experimentation is emerging across domains such as chemistry, biology, and materials, yet each tool class imposes its own execution discipline. Network experimentation requires more than one-shot topology or configuration synthesis: an experimenter must plan a task, operate a live and evolving network, interpret feedback, refine intermediate state, and validate the resulting behavior. This poster presents a Network Experimentation Harness for emulator-backed network experiments, helping LLM agents operate across these stateful workflows. The Harness pairs a semantic action interface with reusable experimentation skills to handle sequencing, timing, and verification that a careful experimenter would perform by hand. A preliminary study on GNS3-based network protocol experiments shows that this approach reduces wall-clock time by 47% and 37%, and token use by 81% and 76%, on average versus raw GNS3 access and a Python wrapper (GNS3Fy), respectively.

title: Foundations for Multi-Logic Modelling and Supervision of Cyber-Physical IoT Agents
publication: Proceedings 2026 IEEE ACM 8th International Workshop on Software Engineering Research and Practices for the Internet of Things Serp4iot 2026
recovered_title: Foundations for Multi-Logic Modelling and Supervision of Cyber–Physical IoT Agents
v20_recovered_title: Foundations for Multi-Logic Modelling and Supervision of Cyber–Physical IoT Agents
v20_abstract: Over the past decade, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has driven the rise of autonomous software agents across cyber and physical environments, tightly linked with the Internet of Things (IoT). In the cyber domain, agentic AI supports decision-making and information gathering, while AI agents such as belief-desire-intention (BDI) ones manage production and shop-floor systems, often connected to industrial IoT (IIoT) infrastructures. As these agents grow more autonomous and integrated, system complexity and risk will increase. Cyber agents may generate biased or inaccurate results due to hallucinations and shallow reasoning while physical BDI agents face environmental uncertainties from sensor noise and actuator flaws. When combined, these risks can amplify and cause severe failures. Their autonomy should therefore be strengthened using logical frameworks and model-driven engineering, and their operation supervised via rule-based control to ensure safety and reliability. This vision paper proposes a rule-based supervision method to enhance the reliability of agent-based systems both consist of agentic AI and AI agents. By integrating fuzzy, epistemic, subjective, and probabilistic logics within a multi-logic modelling (MLM) framework, the approach supports hybrid reasoning under diverse uncertainties. The MLM framework enables coherent integration of multiple logical perspectives, allowing verification and monitoring of agent behaviour through rule-based control. Ultimately, the goal is to build trustworthy and explainable agent systems via MPM.

title: AutoMETA: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Autonomous Meta-Analysis
publication: Aamas 2026 Proceedings of the 25th International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems
recovered_title: AutoMETA: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Autonomous Meta-Analysis
v20_recovered_title: AutoMETA: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Autonomous Meta-Analysis
v20_abstract: Meta-analysis is a statistical method to draw a conclusion from synthesizing the scientific evidence of multiple similar studies on a common research question. However, its execution requires manual tasks including paper selection, data extraction, and statistical pooling. There has been automation efforts for executing partial or whole tasks in a divide-and-conquer manner by a single or multiple AI agents. Yet, meta-analysis using multiple agents in a decentralized and distributed manner under an explicit and auditable protocol is not examined. We introduce AutoMETA, a system of multiple LLM agents that assigns one agent per subject paper of a target meta-analysis. Each agent extracts page-anchored outcomes, critiques peer outputs, and revises entries before passing the finalized dataset to a non-agent statistical module implementing DerSimonian-Laird random-effects pooling with heterogeneity diagnostics. We compare three systems under identical conditions: a Human reference (published meta-analyses), a Single-LLM pipeline without coordination, and AutoMETA (multi-agent with inter-agent critique). As a case study, we selected meta-analyses papers on cardiology in 2004 (8 out of 15 papers meeting inclusion criteria). AutoMETA achieved a median relative effect-size error of 6.4% against human-authored references, compared to 34.0% for the single-agent baseline, while ablation analysis confirmed that removing critique or protocol enforcement progressively degraded accuracy (12.4%, 25.1%, 28.1%). These findings suggest that structured inter-agent critique and procedural enforcement can yield reliable, reproducible statistical reasoning without relying solely on model capability.

title: Graph of Agentic Thoughts: Bridging Agentic Reasoning and Explainability through Graphs
publication: Cods 2025 Proceedings of 13th ACM Ikdd International Conference on Data Science
recovered_title: Graph of Agentic Thoughts: Bridging Agentic Reasoning and Explainability through Graphs
v20_recovered_title: Graph of Agentic Thoughts: Bridging Agentic Reasoning and Explainability through Graphs
v20_abstract: Personal assistants are becoming increasingly intelligent, capable of making autonomous decisions by reasoning over personalized user contexts. This autonomy, however, brings a growing need for transparency in how decisions are made, especially when such assistants interpret vague or implicit user inputs. The shift from conventional pipeline architectures to agentic systems introduces further challenges, making explainability critical. Traditional explainability approaches either focus on local agent rationales or rely on linear execution logs, which fail to capture the full context of multi-agent collaboration and task flow. To address this gap, we introduce Graph of Agentic Thoughts (GoAT), a graph-based reasoning framework that unifies agent-level decisions, flow-level rationales, memory transitions, and counterfactual paths into a single, queryable graph. Unlike approaches that merely stitch individual agent rationales, GoAT models the entire causal flow and rejected alternatives, allowing large language models (LLMs) to generate faithful and contrastive explanations. This joint reasoning over factual and counterfactual paths enhances trust for end-users and provides developers with debugging insights like delegation chains, memory access patterns and internal interpretations. Tailored explanation modes ensure that developers receive detailed causal traces, while users get simplified justifications grounded in logic with counterfactual reasoning. GoAT achieves notable improvements in Causal Clarity (+1.14), User Trust (+1.07), and Faithfulness (+1), demonstrating the value of structured, graph-based explainability for agentic systems.

title: Is artificial intelligence a good servant but a bad master?
publication: Proceedings of SPIE the International Society for Optical Engineering
recovered_title: Is artificial intelligence a good servant but a bad master?
v20_recovered_title: Is artificial intelligence a good servant but a bad master?
v20_abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly moving from a specialized research topic into a widely deployed general-purpose technology, driven by advances in transformer-based architectures, convincing enough productivity gains, large private investment, geopolitical competition, and expanding educational adoption. AI comprises two distinct sets of methodologies: (i) predictive AI, which is grounded in statistical inference and aims to model measurable physical reality, and (ii) generative AI, which produces plausible synthetic content without intrinsic verification against physical reality. Whereas predictive AI can strengthen human decision-making through rigorously tested models grounded in impeccable mathematics, generative AI introduces systemic risks that extend beyond technical reliability. Generative AI is a wicked problem, because its consequences are deeply entangled across environmental, human, ethical, educational, and cultural domains. Generative AI accelerates energy demand, greenhouse-gas emissions, water consumption, and electronic waste, thereby amplifying environmental burdens. It also intensifies inequality through an expanding AI divide, undermines intellectual property norms, and relies on poorly compensated human labor for ongoing data annotation and content moderation. Furthermore, hallucinated outputs, misinformation, and AI slop degrade epistemic trust in online information ecosystems. Ethical dangers include privacy erosion, algorithmic bias in societal decision-making, and increased risk of catastrophic failures in high-stakes contexts such as policing and warfare. Generative AI may reduce critical thinking in students through cognitive offloading and weaken originality and writing skills. AI may serve as a useful servant to specialists for workflow acceleration but we must reject it for general-purpose use, with strict regulation necessary for public chatbot deployment to preserve human judgment and sustain civilization.

title: Invited: Agentic AI for Physical Design R&D: Status and Prospects
publication: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Physical Design
recovered_title: Invited: Agentic AI for Physical Design R&D: Status and Prospects
v20_recovered_title: Invited: Agentic AI for Physical Design R&D: Status and Prospects
v20_abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and tool-using autonomous agents present new opportunities for accelerating research and development in physical design. Unlike earlier uses of machine learning that focused narrowly on prediction or optimization subroutines, agentic AI systems can comprehend user specifications, modify code, run EDA tools, analyze results, perform multi-step reasoning, and iteratively refine design heuristics. This paper surveys the emerging landscape of agentic AI for physical design R&D, with emphasis on (i) tool-integrated agents for algorithm evolution, debugging, and workflow automation, (ii) autonomous exploration of heuristic spaces in placement, routing, and partitioning, and (iii) interfaces between agents and traditional EDA frameworks. We analyze recent experience with multi-agent workflows and benchmark evaluation, highlighting current capabilities, limitations, and research frontiers. We conclude by articulating the long-term prospects of agentic AI as a catalyst for accelerated innovation in physical design, including autonomous algorithm discovery, continuous tool improvement, and closed-loop learning from large design corpora.

title: AgenticNav: A Hierarchical Multi-Agentic System for LLM-Driven Autonomous Problem-Solving in Robotics
publication: IEEE Access
recovered_title: AgenticNav: A Hierarchical Multi-Agentic System for LLM-Driven Autonomous Problem-Solving in Robotics
v20_recovered_title: AgenticNav: A Hierarchical Multi-Agentic System for LLM-Driven Autonomous Problem-Solving in Robotics
v20_abstract: A primary challenge in autonomous robotics is bridging the semantic-execution gap in environments where pre-defined plans fail. This paper presents AgenticNav, a cognitive architecture that achieves autonomous problem-solving through a hierarchical Multi-Agentic System (MAS) orchestrated by a Large Language Model (LLM). Within this framework, specialized agents handle environmental perception and task execution, while a stateful agentic hierarchy facilitates failure detection and strategic recovery. When an environmental impasse is encountered, the hierarchical mechanism isolates high-level reasoning from low-level execution and escalates the execution failure to a strategic level where the LLM re-evaluates the environment’s topological structure to autonomously generate a viable alternative route. Validated in both a high-fidelity simulation and on a physical robot, the system demonstrates the ability to move beyond rigid instruction-following toward greater goal-oriented autonomy. Our results show evidence that the MAS framework effectively facilitates real-time, reason-based replanning, allowing robots to autonomously resolve complex execution failures in unpredictable real-world settings. The comprehensive evaluation data are available at https://github.com/AgenticNav/mas-llm-robotics-eval

v20_abstract: The use of Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) has received immense focus in that it can effectively manage multistep, complex tasks without human intervention and can bring great opportunities to the process of enterprise automation and decision-making. This paper provides comprehensive information about industrial automation of applications using Agentic AI. A systematic study of agentic systems and classification of the architectures of Agentic systems into single-agent, multi-agent and hybrid architectures is also discussed. Moreover, complete information of the technical stack in a layered format, required to implement Agentic AI systems, is presented. The reputed providers/startups/companies of services/tools are presented in the tech stack. A sectoral analysis of real-world applications and their results is compiled in domains such as manufacturing, financial services and healthcare. Different levels of autonomy and operational gap analysis of industry applications are presented in this research work. The novel trust-verify governance framework and cognitive state transition matrix are also offered and discussed. This research work will act as a ready reference to all researchers, practitioners and engineers who want to design and operationalize autonomous AI agents that are effective, reliable and influential in industry applications.

title: Context-Aware Artificial Intelligence Framework for Automated Clinical Documentation using Advanced Natural Language Processing
publication: Proceedings of the 2026 12th International Conference on Communication and Signal Processing Iccsp 2026
recovered_title: Context-Aware Artificial Intelligence Framework for Automated Clinical Documentation using Advanced Natural Language Processing
v20_recovered_title: Context-Aware Artificial Intelligence Framework for Automated Clinical Documentation using Advanced Natural Language Processing
v20_abstract: Clinical documentation constitutes a substantial and cognitively demanding component of contemporary healthcare practice, requiring practitioners to systematically synthesise patient-physician interactions into structured clinical scribe records with both precision and efficiency. Despite rapid advancements in artificial intelligence and natural language processing, existing automated documentation solutions remain fundamentally limited by inadequate contextual comprehension, rigid template architectures, and the absence of patient-specific grounding collectively contributing to clinically significant documentation errors.This paper presents a context-aware, retrieval-augmented framework for automated clinical documentation, designed to address these deficiencies through three synergistic mechanisms. First, a session-persistent vector knowledge store encodes and indexes transcribed patient-physician interactions, enabling longitudinal context retention across clinical encounters. Second, a dynamic template engine permits real-time, schema-level customisation without necessitating model retraining, thereby accommodating diverse specialty workflows and institutional documentation standards. Third, a modular multi-agent orchestration layer enforces sequential validation, retrieval, reasoning, and generation substantially mitigating hallucination and ensuring that all generated content remains strictly grounded in verified transcript data.The proposed framework achieves end-to-end document gen- eration in under three seconds, rendering it viable for real- time intra-visit deployment. Evaluations demonstrate consistent, factually accurate documentation across multiple clinical note formats, representing a meaningful advancement in automated clinical documentation through transcript-grounded, context- aware, and template-driven generation.

title: An Organization-Scoped LLM Agent Runtime Architecture for Regulated Cybersecurity Operations
publication: Proceedings 2026 22nd International Conference on Distributed Computing in Smart Systems and the Internet of Things Dcoss Iot 2026
recovered_title: An Organization-Scoped LLM Agent Runtime Architecture for Regulated Cybersecurity Operations
v20_recovered_title: An Organization-Scoped LLM Agent Runtime Architecture for Regulated Cybersecurity Operations
v20_abstract: Regulated cybersecurity workflows lack a runtime substrate that enforces organization-level scope across retrieval, tool calls, memory, findings, reports, and audit while remaining model-agnostic and locally deployable. Recent large language model (LLM) agent systems report strong results on isolated cybersecurity tasks, yet they do not by themselves define an auditable platform architecture for regulated security operations centre (SOC) and compliance workflows, where a single analyst may trigger actions that bind the organization, and where the runtime must integrate with existing SIEM/XDR stacks as a primary source of context and alert-driven triggers rather than operate as a standalone analytical layer. This paper proposes an organization-scoped LLM agent runtime architecture for financial cybersecurity. The contribution is a typed Security Context that is created at every entry point—including SIEM/XDR notifications ingested as first-class triggers—and enforced at every component boundary, combined with a shared Runtime Core, logical specialist subagents, a governed Tool Adapter Layer exposing SIEM/XDR query, enrichment, and response primitives under uniform policy and audit, structured findings with evidence references, tiered human-in-the-loop (HITL) gates, and append-only audit. Model Context Protocol (MCP), extended telemetry, digital twins for pentesting, graph retrieval, and federated knowledge sharing are treated as optional extension paths rather than mandatory runtime assumptions. We describe an implementable slice as the architecture’s testability surface, and we propose a falsifiable evaluation plan with metric-level pass criteria for architecture readiness, security-policy enforcement, evidence traceability, output quality, and operational observability.

title: Quality-Driven Agentic Reasoning for LLM-Assisted Software Design: Questions-of-Thoughts (QoT) as a Time-Series Self-QA Chain
publication: 2026 IEEE International Conference on AI and Data Analytics Icad 2026
recovered_title: Quality-Driven Agentic Reasoning for LLM-Assisted Software Design: Questions-of-Thoughts (QoT) as a Time-Series Self-QA Chain
v20_recovered_title: Quality-Driven Agentic Reasoning for LLM-Assisted Software Design: Questions-of-Thoughts (QoT) as a Time-Series Self-QA Chain
v20_abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have accelerated AI-assisted software development, yet practical deployment remains constrained by incomplete implementations, weak modularization, and inconsistent security practices. We introduce Questions-of-Thoughts (QoT), a quality-driven inferencetime scaffold that turns a user goal into (i) an ordered sequence of engineering steps and (ii) stepwise self-questioning to verify constraints and reduce omission errors, while maintaining a lightweight reasoning record that stabilizes subsequent design decisions.We evaluate QoT across three representative backend engineering domains: API Design, Data Communication, and File Systems. Each task requires multi-module decomposition and exposes standard failure modes in LLM-generated systems. To enable data-driven comparison, we score generated artifacts using an ISO/IEC-inspired quality rubric that measures Scalability, Completeness, Modularity, and Security. We report domain-wise gains as the change in total quality score, defined as the QoT score minus the NoQoT score. Results show capacity-dependent improvements: QoT yields consistent quality improvements for larger models and more complex domains, while smaller models may exhibit trade-offs under tight context and planning budgets. We release an open artifact with prompts, scoring guidelines, raw generations, and scripts that reproduce the reported tables and figures to support applied AI and data analytics research.

title: Intention Recognition Method of High Orbit Spatial Targets Based on Large Language Model Agents
publication: Proceedings 2026 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Big Data Science and Engineering Icbdse 2026
recovered_title: Intention Recognition Method of High Orbit Spatial Targets Based on Large Language Model Agents
v20_recovered_title: Intention Recognition Method of High Orbit Spatial Targets Based on Large Language Model Agents
v20_abstract: With the increasing frequency and complexity of high-orbit space activities, achieving accurate identification of the behavioral intention of the target spacecraft has become the key to improving space situational awareness and ensuring space traffic safety. This paper proposes a method for identifying the behavioral intention of high-orbit spatial targets based on large language model agents, which realizes a complete cognitive chain from original orbital observation data to behavior recognition and intention inference by constructing cognitive agents with tool calling capabilities. The agent combines domain knowledge prompts, orbit prediction tools, behavior recognition tools, and payload feasible working window calculation tools to complete the hierarchical collaboration of numerical calculation and semantic reasoning. The results show that the Qwen3.6-Plus model performs the best in the behavioral intention recognition task, with a recognition accuracy of 91.67%. Experiments verify the effectiveness and interpretability of the proposed method in the recognition of complex behaviors in high-orbit space, and provide a technical basis for the construction of a scalable and highly reliable spatial situation cognition system.

title: RadAgents: Multimodal Agentic Reasoning for Chest X-ray Interpretation with Radiologist-like Workflows
publication: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research
v20_recovered_title: RadAgents: Multimodal Agentic Reasoning for Chest X-ray Interpretation with Radiologist-like Workflows
v20_abstract: Agentic systems offer a potential path to solve complex clinical tasks through collaboration among specialized agents, augmented by tool use and external knowledge bases. Nevertheless, for chest X-ray (CXR) interpretation, prevailing methods remain limited: (i) reasoning is frequently neither clinically interpretable nor aligned with guidelines, reflecting mere aggregation of tool outputs; (ii) multimodal evidence is insufficiently fused, yielding text-only rationales that are not visually grounded; and (iii) systems rarely detect or resolve cross-tool inconsistencies and provide no principled verification mechanisms. To bridge the above gaps, we present RadAgents, a multi-agent framework that couples clinical priors with task-aware multimodal reasoning and encodes a radiologist-style workflow into a modular, auditable pipeline. In addition, we integrate grounding and multimodal retrieval-augmentation to verify and resolve context conflicts, resulting in outputs that are more reliable, transparent, and consistent with clinical practice.

title: Authenticated and Offline-Verifiable Agent-to-Agent Messaging for LLM Agents
publication: 2026 IEEE 16th Annual Computing and Communication Workshop and Conference Ccwc 2026
recovered_title: Authenticated and Offline-Verifiable Agent-to-Agent Messaging for LLM Agents
v20_recovered_title: Authenticated and Offline-Verifiable Agent-to-Agent Messaging for LLM Agents
v20_abstract: The latest A2A systems often use LLM-based agents for tool calling and planning workflows, introducing risks such as prompt injection attacks. We introduce a lightweight, proof-carrying receipt for agent-to-agent (A2A) messaging that supports fully offline verification. This receipt enables third parties to verify who authored a message and confirm whether it was logged, without contacting the sender, the receiver, or any online service. An agent signs a canonical JSON representation of each message. Servers log the payload hash in a Merkle tree and periodically sign the tree state as a Signed Tree Head (STH). The returned bundle includes a receipt containing a Merkle proof, an STH, and a minimal decentralized identifier (DID) registry for offline key discovery. A verifier recomputes the Merkle root and validates the payload-hash match, Merkle inclusion, and both the STH and client signatures entirely offline. In our prototype, the proof size grows as $O(\log N)$, and the median offline verification time is approximately 0.4 s on our test platform. Receipts self-authenticate individual messages within a single transparency log, providing a lightweight alternative to other approaches.

title: MCSafe-GSN-HOL: A Formal Assurance Framework for Machine-Checkable Safety Cases of Deployed LLM Agents
publication: Proceedings of the International Conference on Circuit Power and Computing Technologies Iccpct 2026
recovered_title: MCSafe-GSN-HOL: A Formal Assurance Framework for Machine-Checkable Safety Cases of Deployed LLM Agents
v20_recovered_title: MCSafe-GSN-HOL: A Formal Assurance Framework for Machine-Checkable Safety Cases of Deployed LLM Agents
v20_abstract: Deployed large language model (LLM) agents are now being used to interface with external tools, fetch information, run code, interact with user data and help with decision making at the workflow level. Therefore, their safety issues are not only related to the underlying model, but also to tool permissions, prompt design, retrieval sources, policy constraints, evidence validity, and varying operational contexts. While Goal Structuring Notation (GSN) has become a popular means of structuring safety arguments, many GSN-based safety cases are still reliant on manual inspection and can suffer from unsupported goals, incomplete evidence paths, undischarged assumptions, circular arguments, unaddressed defeaters, or insufficient coverage of hazards. This paper introduces MCSafe-GSN-HOL, a formal assurance framework for creating machine-checkable safety cases for deployed LLM agents that overcomes these disadvantages. The proposed framework translates the structured GSN arguments into Isabelle/HOL proof obligations, and formalizes the typed GSN elements, the hazard contracts of LLM-agents, the evidence-completeness conditions, the assumption-discharge rules, the defeater-resolution rules, and the incremental re-verification rules after deployment changes. The prototype was tested with 25 safety-case fragments from five representative scenarios of LLM-agents. Results demonstrate that MCSafe-GSN-HOL has 97.3% defect detection, 97.2% evidence coverage, 96.4% hazard-control coverage, and 62.7% reduction in review time compared to manual GSN review. The mean Isabelle/HOL checking time was 2.53 s/safety case, showing that theorem-prover supported assurance can still be practical for medium scale safety-case checking. The results overall support the conclusion that formally checked GSN safety cases can help with the traceability, auditability, consistency and maintainability of assurance processes for deployed LLM-agent systems.

title: Verifier-Guided Autonomous SQL Generation Using LLM Agents and Schema-Aware Retrieval
publication: 2026 International Conference on Cybersecurity Digital Forensics and AI Applications Iccsdfai 2026
recovered_title: Verifier-Guided Autonomous SQL Generation Using LLM Agents and Schema-Aware Retrieval
v20_recovered_title: Verifier-Guided Autonomous SQL Generation Using LLM Agents and Schema-Aware Retrieval
v20_abstract: Most enterprise databases are queried through SQL, but writing correct SQL requires technical knowledge that many users do not have. Natural language interfaces solve this by converting plain questions into SQL automatically. Current systems have made good progress on standard benchmarks, but they still fail in one important way: they check whether a query runs without error, but they do not check whether it actually answers what the user asked. A query can execute cleanly and still return wrong results. This paper presents SEVA-SQL, a system that addresses this problem through two design choices. First, a dual verification stage is applied after every generation step. It runs an execution check and also computes a Semantic Alignment Score (SAS) that measures how closely the generated SQL matches the original question at the meaning level. Second, schema retrieval is made iterative. When a failure is detected, the system uses the error signal to update the retrieval query and fetch a better schema context before trying again. Experiments on the BIRD benchmark show that SEVA-SQL reaches 77.3% execution accuracy, an SAS of 0.84, and a verification round rate of 1.4, all of which are the best results among five recent baselines. On the Spider test set, the system scores 87.6%. These results show that pairing semantic verification with adaptive schema retrieval produces more reliable SQL generation than execution-only correction methods.

title: CAIP-Pentest: A Causal and Interpretable Agent Framework for Autonomous Web Vulnerability Exploration
publication: 2026 International Conference on Cybersecurity Digital Forensics and AI Applications Iccsdfai 2026
recovered_title: CAIP-Pentest: A Causal and Interpretable Agent Framework for Autonomous Web Vulnerability Exploration
v20_recovered_title: CAIP-Pentest: A Causal and Interpretable Agent Framework for Autonomous Web Vulnerability Exploration
v20_abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into cybersecurity has enabled autonomous agents capable of dynamic vulnerability exploration. However, existing agent frameworks (e.g., ReAct, AutoGPT) operate with implicit reasoning, producing decisions that are largely opaque and difficult to audit. We introduce CAIP-Pentest, a framework that structures autonomous penetration testing through an explicit causal decision loop: Observation → Hypothesis → Action → Result (O-H-A-R). By design, every action is justified by a verifiable security hypothesis, enabling full traceability and native interpretability. We formalize the agent’s reasoning as a dynamic Causal Attack Graph and validate the framework via a lightweight Proof of Concept. Experimental results from a proof-of-concept evaluation conducted on OWASP Juice Shop and DVWA across six vulnerability scenarios suggest that CAIP-Pentest maintains competitive exploration coverage while achieving significantly higher interpretability scores than baseline approaches while providing structurally auditable decision traces, addressing a critical gap between LLM autonomy and cybersecurity accountability.

title: Social Engineering of AI Agents
publication: European Conference on Information Warfare and Security Eccws
v20_recovered_title: Social Engineering of AI Agents
v20_abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded within autonomous agents that plan, reason, and interact with external systems through tools such as APIs, databases, and web services. These tool integrations allow agents to overcome the static and outdated nature of LLM knowledge, granting them real-time access to dynamic information sources and operational capabilities as demonstrated in frameworks like ReAct and MRKL. However, this architectural shift also exposes a new and insufficiently understood attack surface. Prior cybersecurity threats targeting application interfaces—such as SQL injection—have relied on injecting structured malicious commands into well-defined syntactic channels. In contrast, LLM agents operate primarily through natural language: both internal planning and external tool selection are mediated linguistically rather than programmatically. This change has profound security implications. Agent behaviour relies heavily on informal language and semantic interpretation. Traditional attack detection fails because it requires rigid markers like command prefixes or specific character patterns. Adversaries exploit this vulnerability by subtly altering the context the agent considers trustworthy. Recent work on tool metadata manipulation demonstrates how adversaries can exploit linguistic cues, authority signals, and persuasive descriptions to influence which tools an agent selects for a task. By modifying tool descriptions—while the tool’s programmed functionality is opaque to the agent—attackers can induce the agent to route sensitive data or actions to malicious endpoints without any direct prompt injection, code execution, or user deception. It is argued that such attacks constitute a new form of machine-targeted social engineering. Traditionally, it is seen that social engineering exploits cognitive biases in humans as the “weakest link” in security. Here, the weakness emerges instead from the ambiguity, informality, and contextual nature of natural language reasoning inside autonomous agents. The agent can be persuaded into harmful behaviour. It is discussed how such threats can be categorized within emerging agent security frameworks such as OWASP and MAESTRO, and defensive strategies designed to safeguard tool-using LLM systems from intentional manipulation are outlined. The findings indicate that cognitive security must now extend beyond users to the autonomous systems increasingly acting on their behalf.

title: Customizable Runtime Enforcement of Safe and Reliable LLM Agents for Future Unsafe States
publication: 2026 International Conference on System Computation Automation and Networking Icscan 2026
recovered_title: Customizable Runtime Enforcement of Safe and Reliable LLM Agents for Future Unsafe States
v20_recovered_title: Customizable Runtime Enforcement of Safe and Reliable LLM Agents for Future Unsafe States
v20_abstract: Autonomous LLM agents now routinely manipulate file systems and APIs in high-stakes software engineering workflows. While reactive frameworks like AgentSpec monitor individual actions, they fail to account for unsafe outcomes that emerge only from a cumulative sequence of individually compliant steps. This survey analyzes LLM safety across four methodological areas, identifying a fundamental disconnect between a single action enforcement and the reality of multi- stage exploits. We find that the field lacks not only proactive, sequence- level mechanisms for code agents but also the formal probabilistic models required to bound stochastic behavior and behavioral drift. Moreover, current benchmarks are shown to be predominantly static, failing to capture the complexity of real-world trajectories. By mapping these systemic gaps, we define the requirements for a proactive safety roadmap, emphasizing the transition toward dynamic, sequence-aware enforcement and multi-step evaluation metrics to secure agents in production environments.

title: Rollback Is Not Undo: Path-Dependent Failures in LLM-Arbitrated Network Control
publication: Proceedings IEEE INFOCOM
recovered_title: Rollback Is Not Undo: Path-Dependent Failures in LLM-Arbitrated Network Control
v20_recovered_title: Rollback Is Not Undo: Path-Dependent Failures in LLM-Arbitrated Network Control
v20_abstract: AI components are rapidly entering network control planes: LLM agents interpret telemetry, propose mitigations, and a learned arbitrator selects actions. Operationally, such systems inherit a familiar safety valve from traditional networking: protocol rollback. A common assumption is that reverting a patch restores behavior. We show this assumption can fail in AI-augmented control loops. We study an online, closed-loop setting where two LLM agents propose conflicting actions and an LLM arbitrator executes a single decision each round. We formalize protocol paths and introduce a post-rollback recovery metric, the recovery gap, which compares post-rollback performance against a baseline that never experienced the patch. Even when the post-rollback protocol text is identical, the system can exhibit persistent degradation, consistent with path dependence arising from both stateful network trajectories and history-dependent in-context arbitration. Empirically, we instantiate a multi-LLM edge DDoS mitigation task with realistic transient fault modes (observation corruption, delay/reordering, agent dropout, and proposal corruption). Across these perturbations, we observe nontrivial and directionally asymmetric recovery gaps after rollback. Finally, we propose a lightweight mitigation that improves absolute post-rollback cost, though the relative recovery gap persists.

The benchmark instruments tool activations and forwards tool-trigger events to an external Arduino-driven servo actuator, providing physical verification of actuation events. To demonstrate the benchmark in practice, we evaluate eight representative LLMs using 350 executable scenarios: 250 adversarial tests spanning five smart-environment domains (smart home, healthcare IoT, industrial control, public infrastructure, and smart building), 50 capability checks, and 50 benign over-refusal tests. Responses are scored by two independent judge models and verified by a human evaluator. We report Evilness as the extent to which attacks succeed. The Evilness Score equals the number of successful attacks, and the Evilness Rate is the corresponding percentage. Across models, Evilness Rates range from 0.8% to 54.0% (2–135 successful attacks out of 250), while Defense Rates range from 46.0% to 99.2%. The current AI-based solutions in this domain operate through open-loop analytics, where human engagement is required to perform Root Cause Analysis (RCA) of faults, which may take multiple hours. Every minute spent on fault detection is a minute late for corrective action. Until now, industries have implemented pre-programmed fault detection with significant human intervention to diagnose faults and take corrective actions. However, with the evolution of large language models (LLMs) and reasoning models, fault detection can be made autonomous. This research develops an innovative system concept that uses LLMs-orchestrated by a Semantic Kernel as a central reasoning agent to achieve near-closed-loop control in PV manufacturing, allowing autonomous diagnosis and fault handling. This study uses synthetic data based on high-efficiency PV specifications to introduce 50 different anomalies that affect conveyor-based production stages, which would consequently result in low productivity and less efficient PV modules. The LLM agent performed a complete 50-step troubleshooting process to detect efficiency loss causes while creating detailed natural-language reports and recommending specific corrective actions for technicians or robotic systems. The system demonstrated 90% accuracy in root-cause identification through 250 experimental trials using ground-truth anomaly validation when it received a 50-step troubleshooting protocol. The research fills essential gaps in current PV manufacturing automation by tracking defects semantically throughout production stages while providing specific decisions and converting machine data into actionable language-based workflows. The proposed LLM-mediated architecture establishes a major advancement toward adaptive quality assurance systems that operate efficiently and at scale for solar panel production.

v20_abstract: Procure-to-Pay (P2P) automation is essential for enhancing overall enterprise efficiency. Yet, existing systems face several challenges such as inconsistent policy enforcement, audit readiness, and operational inefficiencies, especially in multi-stakeholder environments. These issues and complexities hinder smooth integration and effective process optimization. Current research lacks a comprehensive framework to address these issues in a fully scalable, adaptable, and operationally sound manner. This study designs and validates a novel governance-aligned AI framework that integrates policy-as-code, object-centric analysis, and continuous monitoring to ensure consistent policy enforcement, compliance, and audit readiness. The methodology combines structured stakeholder interviews, an integrative literature review, and systematic model development, followed by a rigorous and thorough proof-of-concept evaluation using synthetic P2P scenarios. Performance results from 30 independent trials show two key findings: the average decision latency is 128.4 milliseconds (σ = 7.6ms), indicating stable performance even under high load, and the framework ensures consistent policy enforcement while providing a tamper-proof audit trail, effectively preventing errors such as double-counting and inconsistent exception handling. These results validate the framework's operational effectiveness and provide a robust, reliable foundation for implementing governance-aligned P2P automation, indicating readiness for real-world deployment across diverse organizational contexts and offering practical insights for future scalability and enhanced policy design.

title: Cross-Agent Multimodal Provenance-Aware Framework for Robust Prompt Injection Defense in Large Language and Vision-Language Models
publication: International Conference on Computer and Applications Icca 2025 Proceedings

v20_recovered_title: Cross-Agent Multimodal Provenance-Aware Framework for Robust Prompt Injection Defense in Large Language and Vision-Language Models
v20_abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs), VisionLanguage Models (VLMs), and new agentic AI systems (e.g., LangChain and GraphChain) allow autonomous systems to reason and plan, and to coordinate between an assortment of tools and agents. Nevertheless, this feature also brings vulnerability to multimodal prompt injection (PI) attacks, in which hidden or malicious instructions that are embedded in text, images, metadata, or interagent messages can spread throughout the agent graph, triggering unintended behavior or policy violation, or corrupting a state. To mitigate these threats, this paper will present a Cross-Agent Multimodal Provenance-Aware Defense Framework that will sanitize any user- or agent-generated prompts and validate the output of the LLM independently, prior to their delivery to downstream nodes. The framework incorporates a text sanitizer agent, visual sanitizer agent and an output validator agent which are synchronized by a provenance ledger which documents modality, source and trust metadata throughout the agent network. The architecture implements ordered trust boundaries, so that an injected instruction cannot spread out via LangChain- or GraphChain-style workflows. There are better multimodal PI detection accuracy, lower trust leakage between agents, and more stable agentic execution pathways, all of which are experimentalized. This framework can build secure, interpretable, and reliable agentic AI systems by augmenting the established provenance tracking and validation systems to multi-agent orchestration.

v20_abstract: Urban policing faces growing challenges in anticipating and mitigating crime amidst dynamic, resource-constrained environments. This paper introduces an agentic AI framework that integrates deep spatio-temporal forecasting with adaptive patrol planning to support proactive public safety strategies. Leveraging over 15 years of crime data from the Seattle Police Department, we train and compare multiple deep learning architectures—including LSTM, GRU, and 1D CNN models—to predict short-term spatial distributions of crime risk. The agentic layer transforms these predictions into autonomous decisions using reinforcement-inspired routing algorithms and a feedback module that refines the predictive model based on observed outcomes. Experimental results demonstrate that GRU-based predictors strike the best balance between accuracy and computational efficiency, while the agent's adaptive planning improves coverage in high-risk zones. We also implement fairness-aware mechanisms to reduce bias in over-policed communities. This study offers one of the first fully integrated frameworks for real-time crime forecasting and patrol decision-making, setting the stage for aligned, adaptive, and ethically responsible AI in law enforcement.

v20_abstract: The main breakthrough in the field of travel management systems is associated with the idea of multi-agent systems that provide personalized, adaptive, and almost fully automated user experiences. As a result, this work introduces a modular multi-agent-based conversational platform which is an interactive and less complicated method of trip planning. The system architecture features mainly a Supervising Agent that is responsible for the coordination of the activities of the specialized sub-agents. The sub-agents are those which handle various domains related to travel. Their implemented operations can each independently perform local data persistence; thus, they ensure session continuity and device stability. The system’s uniqueness lies in the fact that it provides a rollback and conflict-resolution capability to resolve issues autonomously. Powered by a Gemini LLM model for information retrieval, the model provides structured responses to generic user queries related to trip-planning. The decouplable and extensible modular design allows for the proper maintenance and scalability of the system with future extensions to include other sub-agents also made easier and efficient with this design. Hence, the adaptive, agentic design of Trip-Planner is a significant step forward in the area of intelligent travel automation which ultimately results in an excellent user experience through more coordinated activities flow and the seamless end users' engagement.

v20_abstract: Secure and efficient knowledge management based on enterprise chip design and verification documents or bug trackers, pose unique challenges, due to their complex, sensitive, heterogeneous, and multimodal nature. Rapid miniaturization of nodes, sophistication of Intellectual Property (IP)s, and evolution of system-on-chip (SoC) architectures have further added to the demanding scenario, where, within the available enterprise infrastructure, effective solutions have to be developed based on context and requirements of various operational settings. Available state-of-the-art solutions have limited scope of sensitivity to organizational dynamics and smart computational resource planning. In this paper, we present MIRAI- a Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrated Artificial Intelligence (AI) framework that combines language, vision, and structured data understanding through a reflective agentic architecture to provide real-time, contextual and explainable support in Design Verification and Verification (DV&V) tasks. The proposed system has been evaluated across use cases, demonstrating significant gains, i.e., up to 90-95% accuracy in information retrieval, in secure policy information access, AI-based query answering, anomaly detection, debugging, and knowledge mining and functional testing with improved coverage. We believe MIRAI offers a transformative approach to managing and leveraging design data, engineering workflows, and cross-functional team intelligence.

v20_abstract: Biomarker discovery is a key enabler of precision medicine, yet omics analyses, here exemplified by bulk RNA-seq, which remain hampered by ultra-high dimensional data and manual, ad hoc preprocessing. We address the embedding bottleneck by introducing an agentic AI framework that dynamically guides embeddings with pathway knowledge. The agent plans, acts, and verifies in a self-refining loop: profiling data; selecting normalization; choosing an embedding family (a fast linear baseline for rapid iteration and transformer-based encoders as the target representation); and applying quantitative checks (e.g., stability and pathway concordance). Critically, the agent prioritizes pathway sets relevant to the current research focus, adjusting embedding weights or encoder conditioning so the representation emphasizes the most pertinent biology; in this study we demonstrate the mechanism using general pathway resources, while the same orchestration supports focused, disease- or mechanism-specific pathways. The framework is embedding-agnostic and generalizes to multi-omics, aiming to couple statistical representation with biological prior knowledge to improve reproducibility, robustness, and downstream biomarker discovery. We standardize evaluation (splits, seeds, metrics, artifact logging) and show that agent-driven, pathway-guided embeddings provide a stronger substrate for consistent analysis than manual baselines.

v20_abstract: The traditional process of invoice processing is still labor intensive and highly prone to errors; thus, it can result in inefficiency, timeliness and lack of uniformity in financial transactions. The present project is going to solve them by creating an intelligent automated invoice management system by using Robotic Process Automation, Document Understanding, Agent Builder, and UiPath Maestro. The system is also able to automatically access invoices sent via email and extract important information which includes the name of the vendor, invoice number, tax identification, and the amount. It authenticates the extracted information by both the rule-based reasoning and AI-based approaches to get accuracy. The system also does cross-check with the purchase order records to identify inconsistency and directs high value or questionable invoices to the Action Center to be manually approved to keep the balance between automation and human control. The combination of the Agentic AI with the system makes it more intelligent since the system carries out confidence prediction and anomaly detection to guarantee reliability of the extracted data. UiPath Maestro also coordinates and controls the automation process and allows tracking the process in real time, optimizing its performance at the same time. This is a unified amalgamation of new AI and RPA technologies that guarantee quick, transparent, and error-free invoice processing without one intervene. The suggested system will also greatly save processing time, enhance the precision of the data and the robustness of financial management, which proves the transformative power of intelligent automation in business activities.
